title: Route checks by job kind per ci-routing section 3.2
summary: Add a routing function in athena-core that maps a plan's class_of_work to where each check runs (CI-reused versus local) and what the verifier is told, following the 3.2 table. Unknown or missing kind takes the config row. Audience: the Athena maintainer and reviewers of ci-routing.md.

defaults_applied.how: Implementation and tests in Rust in athena-core.
Per-kind routing tests; cargo test and clippy clean.
Criteria check routing outcomes per kind, not that a module exists.
One routing module plus wiring and a design-doc status note.
Criteria tie to checks running in the right place with the right fallback.
Verifier runs cargo test, clippy, fmt --check.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Item 4 is only built in part (resolve exists but is not called from the job run); item 5 builds on that module and wires routing to the job-run path rather than waiting for more of item 4.
Job kind is the plan's class_of_work, taken from the reading.
The producer's edit loop is unchanged; routing moves Athena's checks and the verifier's test run only.
The verifier's allowed commands stay unchanged (section 3.3).
Measurement, cache timing and README/CHANGELOG are later items (6, 7).

acceptance_criteria.text: Run `cargo test -p athena-core routing`: tests assert, for each kind (code, tests, docs, design, config, build, study, other), the routed checks and their skips match the section 3.2 table (docs and design skip fmt/clippy but always run test; config never skips; build adds the workflow's own run and never reuses a prior result).
A test shows a missing or unrecognised job kind gets the config row (all three checks, none skipped), per section 7.
A test shows the routed path calls the item 4 `resolve` with the candidate SHA: a CI result for another SHA is ignored and falls back to a local run; a red CI result fails and does not rerun locally.
`cargo test`, `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check` all pass.
docs/design/ci-routing.md section 10 item 5 is updated to say what was built and what is not done (for example no speedup measured), without claiming a measured improvement.
The routing is used from the job run or verifier input, not only defined: a reader can find the call site that selects checks by the plan's kind.

out_of_scope: Measurement job (item 6) and the docs job (item 7)
Changes to .github/workflows/ci.yml or the verifier's allowed commands
Pushing the candidate commit before the read and the wait-bound value
departures: Slightly higher cost and lower pass chance than reference: item 4 is only partly wired, so the producer must touch the job-run path.
